newsitem.title: UK: New Hanson shares quoted in "grey" market.
newsitem.headline: New Hanson shares quoted in "grey" market.

text.p: Shares in the two stocks being created in the final demerger of conglomerate Hanson Plc began trading on Tuesday in a "grey" market prior to the official demerger due to take place next week.

Shares in "new" Hanson Plc, a building materials group, were quoted at 303-1/2p by 0959 GMT while Energy Group Plc, which includes Eastern Electricity in the U.K. and Peabody Coal in the U.S., were quoted at 543p.
Hanson shares were up 1-1/2p at 92 in active trade of 2.8 million shares. "The price of the two stocks is pretty much as we had expected," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
"It has been a long time coming and the question now is whether anyone else is going to break up in this kind of way."

The final Hanson spin-off, due to be voted on at an extraordinary general meeting on Friday, will complete a process begun almost two years ago. Imperial Tobacco Plc and Millennium Chemicals were spun off last October.

Energy Group and new Hanson shares will make their formal market debut next Monday. Yet while Energy Group is poised to gain a place in the FTSE 100, Hanson -- at its height one of the UK's biggest industrial groups -- will likely lose its position in the blue chip index.
Analysts said the verdict on the controversial demerger was still mixed. "If you reconsituted the various bits you would find that the demerger has destroyed quite a lot of value," said one.
